summary: Yoichi Kawada works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He served as Director of The Institute of Oriental Philosophy, a post attested in 2002 and 2016.
Yong Hua works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tengchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries, served as lopön at Menri and Triten Norbutse, and was a visiting scholar at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Palpung Sherabling Monastery and the Dzongsar Institute under teachers including Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, later serving as abbot at Palpung Sherabling around 1998.
Yongshan He specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University under James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at Tsinghua and Harvard, he held professorships at Southeast, National Central, and Peking universities, later serving as vice-president of Peking University in 1949 and 1951.

Yonten Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a Diplôme at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as a research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. A Kyoto University graduate, he held teaching posts at Kobe Women's University (1989–2004), Bukkyo University (research assistant in 1980; professor in 2014), and Otani University (attested 2010).

Yoshifumi Mizuno works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, later serving as an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1986–1992) and associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University under Shoson Miyamoto and Shigeo Kamata, and later served on Komazawa's faculty as a lecturer in 1971 and professor in 2001.
Yoshihiko Amino was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (1947–1953). He held academic posts at Nagoya University (1967–1980) and Kanagawa University (1980–1999).

Yoshihiko Nasu works in Buddhist studies. He has served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held positions at Social Welfare Corporation Kongojushinkai and Kongoju (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001), where he also served as a lecturer (attested 2003), and worked as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Research Center.
Yoshihiro Matsunami is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor (attested 1991–1999) and later as president (2001) of Taisho University.

Yoshihito Muroji works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, served as an assistant at Kyoto University, and held faculty posts at Koyasan University and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiko Shimabukuro studied in the fields of Buddhist studies and religious studies, attending Kyoto Chuo Bukkyo Gakuen until 1936 and Kyoto Women's University from 1936 to 1940.

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He held academic posts at Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993–2000), served as president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and became a professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

Yoshinobu Sakaide was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from 1953 to 1963 under Mitsuji Fukunaga, and later held a post at Kansai University from around 1969 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe, later serving there as assistant professor (1948) and professor (1959–1976), before joining Aichi Gakuin University (~1977–1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (1941–1944) and under Paul Demiéville (1956–1958), and worked at Kyoto University as a library assistant from around 1949 to 1984.
